note: Built as ballot/lean/mn_endorsements.json is. Each record is one line of one party page, matched to one race and one candidate on the official lists already loaded in ballot_local_2026.sqlite (office, place and name all fit, one fit only). Wisconsin differs from Minnesota: its parties nominate in the August 11 partisan primary and, after it, mostly publish lists of their nominees rather than endorsements. Only a page that itself says 'endorse' is under endorsements (one record). Support in other words (supported, recommended, a list under a sentence about 'endorsed candidates') is under other_support with the page's own word in 'kind', kept apart and not for showing as an endorsement. A bare list of a party's candidates is not collected at all: it adds nothing to the party label already on the ballot. Governor and lieutenant governor are one November ticket, so a page's two lines are one record. Federal offices on these pages are outside this file; so are spring (April) offices. The same candidate stands on several lists: count once per party. Every page in 'lists' was opened again on the day it was read and a record is kept only if the page still showed the name; pages were fetched with the kit's honest User-Agent after checking each site's robots.txt, and a site that forbids programs was not opened (see not_read). Only 10 of Wisconsin's 72 counties have county races loaded, so county endorsements elsewhere cannot match yet.
